about: Test vectors of the document profile de.wappensc.together.format.richtext/1, defined at the address under definition.
updates: Yjs updates in encoding version 1, Base64. Applied to an empty Yjs document in any order, with duplicates, they yield the state described here.
state: that state as one update; stateVector: its state vector; deleted: the canonical encoding of what it deleted; all Base64.

content: the delta of the Y.Text content. A run of characters is a string, an embedded value one insert. In values, a Y.Map is {"map": {...}} with its keys sorted, a Y.Array {"array": [...]}, bytes {"binary": "<Base64>"}, any other JSON value Yjs stores {"json": ...}. attributes are the run's formats.
beside: the names of the top-level shared types other than content.
projection: the plain-text projection; projectionLength: its length in UTF-16 code units.
paragraphs: what a reader shows of each paragraph after normalization: its text (an embed as U+FFFC), block (null for body text), indent, checked, quote, and the number of an ordered list item.
images: for each embed of type image, its unit in content and what a reader shows: the original, the preview, or the fallback.

vectors.name: initial-state
vectors.description: The initial state a creator seeds a new document with: one paragraph end without other keys, that is one empty paragraph. It projects to nothing, since the document's last paragraph end never counts.

vectors.name: paragraphs
vectors.description: Two paragraphs. A writer inserts text before the document's last paragraph end and starts a new paragraph by inserting a paragraph end; the first end projects to a line feed, the last to nothing.

vectors.name: line-break
vectors.description: A line break within a paragraph is the character U+000A in the text. It projects to itself, as a paragraph end does; the reader still sees two paragraphs, the first of two lines.

Roses are red,
violets are blue.

paragraphs.text:

violets are blue.

vectors.name: paragraph-styles
vectors.description: Paragraph styles are keys of the paragraph end: block for headings h1 to h6 and code, quote, and indent, which also applies to body text. The last change sets indent on an existing paragraph end, a change of that Y.Map alone; the projection does not change.

vectors.name: lists
vectors.description: List items: checklist items, done or not, bullets, dashes and ordered items, nested by indent. Numbers follow the numbering rule: start counts at a list's first item, a deeper item nests and does not end the list, a paragraph that is no list item ends it. List markers and checkboxes project to nothing; the last paragraph is empty body text.

vectors.name: formats
vectors.description: Character formats are Yjs text attributes: bold, italic, underline, strike and code with the value true, link with the address as text. A reader opens only https, http and mailto addresses and shows any other link as text, keeping its value. The last change makes "bold" italic too, with Y.Text.format; formats never change the projection.

vectors.name: embed
vectors.description: An embed is a Y.Map with a type and a fallback. A reader that does not know its type shows the fallback as a placeholder and keeps the embed unchanged. Every embed projects to one U+FFFC.

vectors.name: image
vectors.description: An embed of type image: metadata, a JPEG preview, and the original in parts. The writer inserts the embed with its preview first, then appends each part in a change of its own. All parts are there and their SHA-256 matches, so a reader shows the original.

vectors.name: image-parts-missing
vectors.description: The image vector's first two updates only: the embed has arrived with its preview, its parts not yet. A reader shows the preview until the original is complete.

vectors.name: unknown-and-out-of-range
vectors.description: What a reader does not know it keeps unchanged: an unknown block value and paragraph key, an unknown format, a known format with an unknown value, an image of an unknown type, and a format on a paragraph end. Values out of range count as absent: indent only from 1 to 8 and only on list items and body text, checked only on a checklist item, start only at an ordered list's first item. The name example is never defined by this profile.

vectors.name: table-cells
vectors.description: Paragraph ends with the keys table, row and col end table cells. A cell's end projects to a tab when the next paragraph end is a cell of the same table and row, else to a line feed; the document's last end still projects to nothing. Until tables are defined further, a reader shows each cell as a paragraph.

Before
A	B
C	D
After
E	F

vectors.name: concurrent
vectors.description: Three writers. Bob and Carol, each holding Alice's two updates, insert at the same place and set block on the same paragraph end at the same time. Applied in any order, the updates yield one state: Yjs orders the two insertions, and of the two values of block one wins, the same for every replica.

vectors.name: deletions
vectors.description: Deleting text, then the paragraph end between two paragraphs, which joins them: the joined paragraph has the keys of the end that remains, here none. The state's deleted items are what the canonical encoding of deletions lists.

vectors.name: utf-16
vectors.description: Offsets count UTF-16 code units: a character outside the Basic Multilingual Plane counts two, a combining accent one of its own.

vectors.name: beside-content
vectors.description: Beside content: a layer, a top-level type named by a layer id (com.example.notes/1), and a top-level type that no layer id names (scratch), which breaks the structure. Neither is part of the projection; a reader keeps both.

vectors.name: after-the-last-end
vectors.description: A writer that breaks the structure inserts text after the last paragraph end. A reader still applies and keeps it: the text after the last end is a paragraph of its own, without an end, and since the last unit is no paragraph end, every paragraph end projects to a line feed.
